newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's bank shares up on land hopes, buy-backs.
newsitem.headline: Japan's bank shares up on land hopes, buy-backs.

text.p: Japanese bank shares rose on Monday morning, spurred by hopes that the government will announce measures to boost the sluggish property market and due to buying back ahead of the end of the fiscal year, brokers said.
At 0117 GMT, Sakura Bank Ltd was up 47 yen at 838 yen. Its share volume of 4.911 million was ranked as the second heaviest on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd rose 80 yen to 2,120 yen. Fuji Bank Ltd was up 120 yen at 1,610 yen. Sumitomo Bank Ltd gained 100 yen to 1,690 yen.

Banking and construction shares have been bouncing back since last week, heartened by newspaper reports that the government may use public funds to buy land formerly owned by failed housing loan firms and other troubled financial institutions.
Banks have been unable to unload some of their collateralised property holdings due to the weak real estate market.
